newsitem.title: UK: BA sacks union boss after "fat cat" fight.
newsitem.headline: BA sacks union boss after "fat cat" fight.

text.p: British Airways Plc confirmed on Tuesday that the head of the airline's biggest cabin crew union was fired for assaulting another employee, following a row over allegations of being a "fat cat" union boss.

Mike Coleman, the branch secretary of the British Airlines Stewards and Stewardesses Association (BASSA) was accused of hitting Dave Fallon, an official with the smaller rival union Cabin Crew 89, after he caught Fallon handing out copies of a newspaper article about him to fellow workers at BA's London Heathrow headquarters.
A Daily Mirror story in January said Coleman earned over 100,000 pounds last year, making him Britain's highest paid union boss, despite representing only 9,000 people at BA.

Headlined "Brother Fat Cat", the article said Coleman had supplemented his 32,000 pounds salary from BA with 50,000 pounds in annual commissions on union membership subscriptions and 20,000 in daily expense allowances.
"People have got a grudge but I have nothing to hide. I work hard for our members," Coleman was quoted as saying.
BA said on Tuesday that Coleman had been dismissed as the result of a disciplinary hearing, and lost his appeal last Friday.
"We can confirm that Mr Mike Coleman, a senior member of cabin crew and the airline's branch secretary of cabin crew union BASSA, has been dismissed," a spokesman said.

"An internal disciplinary hearing in February found allegations that he had physically assaulted another employee on company premises to be substantiated. The final appeal under the company's disciplinary procedures has upheld this original decision," he said.
"Physical assault is considered gross misconduct for which dismissal is the appropriate sanction."

The spokeman said the union had been kept informed and representatives were present during the disciplinary process. No one at the Transport and General Workers' Untion (the T&G) to which BASSA is affiliated was available for comment.
Coleman could not be contacted for comment either.
